target.title: fix(infra): enforce maxBytes in readResponseBodySnippet non-streaming fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseBodySnippet` in `src/infra/http-error-body.ts` has a non-streaming fallback path (when the response body lacks a reader) that calls `response.text()` without any size limit. The entire response body is buffered into memory before the `maxBytes` check is applied, creating an OOM risk for large error responses.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply `maxBytes` via `TextEncoder → subarray(maxBytes) → TextDecoder` in the non-streaming path, matching the streaming path's byte-bound enforcement. Strip trailing replacement characters (U+FFFD) so a subarray cut that lands mid-codepoint does not leak bare replacement characters into the snippet.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (9/9 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_response_body_snippet_bound.mts

PASS  non-streaming: snippet ≤ maxChars :: len=200 max=500
PASS  non-streaming: byte length ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=200 max=200
PASS  non-streaming small: passes through :: got="hello"
PASS  streaming: snippet ≤ maxChars :: len=200 max=500
PASS  streaming: byte length ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=200 max=200
PASS  streaming small: passes through :: got="world"
PASS  multibyte non-streaming: bytes ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=15 max=15
PASS  multibyte non-streaming: chars ≤ maxChars :: chars=5 max=100
PASS  multibyte non-streaming: no replacement character :: snippet="啊啊啊啊啊"

[proof] 9 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

The proof calls the actual `readResponseBodySnippet` function with mock Response objects that trigger the non-streaming fallback, verifying maxBytes/maxChars enforcement and multibyte UTF-8 safety.

## Issue

Fixes #101269
